title: Mineral Deposition in Bacteria-Filled and Bacteria-Free Calcium Bodies in the Crustacean Hyloniscus riparius (Isopoda: Oniscidea)
raman_evidence: PDF p.11 (Fig. 9C): calcite peaks at 1086 (nu1), 713 (nu4), 155 and 280 cm-1 (lattice) in the anterior calcium bodies
sample_description: Calcite-containing mineralised matrix in the calcium bodies of the isopod Hyloniscus riparius (other bodies contain apatite); FT-Raman
notes: FT-Raman with 1064 nm excitation (Bruker Ramanscope III, Ge detector), so low fluorescence. SI are two TIFF figures (S1, S2).

title: Limpet Shells from the Aterian Level 8 of El Harhoura 2 Cave (Témara, Morocco): Preservation State of Crossed-Foliated Layers
raman_evidence: PDF p.8: calcite identified by T 155 (translation), L 282 (libration), nu4 711 and nu1 1085 cm-1; Figs. 6 and 7 map the L/nu1 intensity ratio to show changes of calcite crystallographic orientation between lamellae
sample_description: Modern and fossil Patella limpet shell calcite (crossed-foliated layers) from Aterian cave deposits; confocal Raman maps
notes: Orientation-sensitive L/nu1 ratio map (Lc/nu1) in biogenic calcite. WITec alpha300R, 532 nm (the 488 nm laser in the paper is for fluorescence imaging). No SI.

title: Occlusion of Sulfate-Based Diblock Copolymer Nanoparticles within Calcite: Effect of Varying the Surface Density of Anionic Stabilizer Chains
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
raman_evidence: PDF p.4 and SI Fig. S5: Raman bands at 154 and 280 (lattice modes), 712 (nu4) and 1086 (nu1) cm-1 for the calcite control and the copolymer/calcite nanocomposite
sample_description: Calcite single crystals with occluded sulfate-based diblock copolymer nanoparticles and a calcite control
notes: Renishaw 2000 Raman microscope, 785 nm diode laser (from the SI). The numbers are read from SI Fig. S5 and the main text. SI PDF included.

title: Experimental and visual research on the microbial induced carbonate precipitation by Pseudomonas aeruginosa
raman_evidence: PDF p.4 (Fig. 3a): precipitate spectrum matches calcite with main peak at 1088 cm-1, in-plane bending at 712 cm-1 and lattice mode at 153 cm-1; a calcite standard is shown in Fig. 3b
sample_description: CaCO3 precipitated in Pseudomonas aeruginosa biofilms (microbially induced carbonate precipitation) in a flow cell; confocal Raman
notes: Princeton Instruments TriVista CRS, 514 nm Ar+ laser, 100x. Only three numbers. SI doc included.

title: Potential Fossilized Sulfide-Oxidizing Bacteria in the Upper Miocene Sulfur-Bearing Limestones From the Lorca Basin (SE Spain): Paleoenvironmental Implications
raman_evidence: PDF p.8 (Fig. 5): low-Mg calcite with typical peaks at 1088, 285, 158 and 713 cm-1; sparry cement (spectrum a) at 1085, 281, 154 and 711 cm-1
sample_description: Upper Miocene sulfur-bearing limestone (Lorca Basin): microsparitic calcite, clotted micrite and sparry calcite cement
notes: Two sets of calcite positions (diagenetic phases) with 4 cm-1 spectral resolution (80 mW, 600 grooves/mm). No SI.

title: The role of chitin-rich skeletal organic matrix on the crystallization of calcium carbonate in the crustose coralline alga Leptophytum foecundum
raman_evidence: PDF p.4 (Fig. 4): MCR components with Raman peaks of calcite (1086, 711, 284 and 158 cm-1) and aragonite (1082, 700, 279, 205, 150); averaged spectra show the 1087 to 1083 cm-1 shift between calcite and aragonite areas
sample_description: Skeleton of the crustose coralline alga Leptophytum foecundum (calcite and aragonite); confocal Raman imaging with MCR analysis
notes: SI states Thermo DXRxi with 455 or 532 nm laser and an NT-MDT system with 532 nm; the paper does not say which laser gave Fig. 4, so both are listed. SI PDF included.

title: Ps19, a novel chitin binding protein from Pteria sterna capable to mineralize aragonite plates in vitro
raman_evidence: PDF p.9: calcite active modes at 282.47, 712.48 and 1087.27 cm-1; aragonite at 206.1, 702.595 and 1085.16 cm-1
sample_description: In vitro CaCO3 crystals (calcite and aragonite) grown with the chitin-binding protein Ps19 of Pteria sterna
notes: Renishaw InVia, 532 nm YAG, 100 mW. Companion paper from the same lab with the same calcite numbers: Rivera-Perez 2020 (10.1038/s41598-020-77320-7) was not added. SI: 3 TIFF figures and one PDF.

title: Geochemistry and Microtextures of Vein Calcites Pervading the Izu‐Bonin Forearc and Rear Arc Crust: New Insights From IODP Expeditions 352 and 351
raman_evidence: PDF p.8 (Fig. 3): calcites show minor peaks at 156-160, 285-287 and 715 cm-1 and major peak at 1087-1089 cm-1
sample_description: Vein calcites from IODP 351/352 Izu-Bonin forearc and rear-arc crust (thin sections, calcite with minor phillipsite/harmotome and goethite)
notes: Geological calcite; positions as ranges over many veins. 532 nm 100 mW Nd:YAG, 100x objective. Source of the T/L/nu4 values also cited to Frezzotti et al. 2012 but the spectra are the authors' own. No SI.

title: Adsorption of Remazol Brilliant Violet-5R Textile Dye from Aqueous Solutions by Using Eggshell Waste Biosorbent
raman_evidence: PDF p.7: calcite bands at 154-155, 280-281, 712 and 1087 cm-1 in untreated and treated eggshell; PDF p.3: palisade layer at 282, 712 and 1087 cm-1
sample_description: Eggshell powder biosorbent (calcite palisade layer), untreated and after dye adsorption; confocal Raman
notes: Horiba LabRAM HR, 532 nm Nd:YAG, 1800 grooves/mm. SI docx included.

title: Geochemical Characterization of the NWA 11273 Lunar Meteorite Using Nondestructive Analytical Techniques: Original, Shocked, and Alteration Mineral Phases
raman_evidence: PDF p.6 (Fig. 6A): Raman bands at 280, 711 and 1087 cm-1 corresponding to calcite; PDF p.7: Raman image of calcite from the 1082-1093 cm-1 interval (main band 1084)
sample_description: Calcite in cracks of the NWA 11273 lunar meteorite (alteration phase), mapped by micro-Raman
notes: Renishaw inVia with 785 and 532 nm lasers (785 nm, 10% power, 50x for the maps). Three calcite numbers. SI PDF included.

title: Sequential SEM-EDS, PLM, and MRS Microanalysis of Individual Atmospheric Particles: A Useful Tool for Assigning Emission Sources
raman_evidence: PDF p.16 (Fig. 13E): prismatic Ca-rich particle with bands at 152.9, 278, 714.4 and 1087.6 cm-1 associated with CaCO3; PDF p.9 (Fig. 5E): CaCO3 bands at 280.5, 711.9 and 1086.2 cm-1 in a Zr-silicate spheroidal particle
sample_description: Individual atmospheric particles (soil resuspension, prismatic CaCO3 particles) analysed by SEM-EDS, polarised light microscopy and micro-Raman
notes: Two calcite-bearing particle types with positions given to 0.1 cm-1 (the second is a mixed particle with ZrSiO4). Horiba LabRAM HR Evolution, 40 mW, 532 nm. SI PDF included.

title: Wasted Biomaterials from Crustaceans as a Compliant Natural Product Regarding Microbiological, Antibacterial Properties and Heavy Metal Content for Reuse in Blue Bioeconomy: A Preliminary Study
raman_evidence: PDF p.5: crab shell calcite bands at 156, 281, 712 and 1085 cm-1 plus ACC band at 1076 cm-1, area ratio A(1085)/A(1076) = 2.44; Fig. 2 caption: crab shell 532 nm, synthetic calcite 1064 nm
sample_description: Crab shell (calcite with amorphous calcium carbonate and phosphate, chitin) from waste crustaceans; synthetic calcite recorded at 1064 nm for comparison
notes: Two excitation wavelengths (532 nm for shell, 1064 nm for the synthetic calcite reference spectrum, numbers for the latter only on the figure). Renishaw inVia Reflex. SI zip holds one supplementary PDF.

title: When Red Turns Black: Influence of the 79 AD Volcanic Eruption and Burial Environment on the Blackening/Darkening of Pompeian Cinnabar
raman_evidence: PDF p.4: calcite bands at 155, 711 and 1086 cm-1 in cinnabar layers and mortar; PDF p.3: calcite 1087 cm-1 in spectra of samples ATT2007/14 and 16/56
sample_description: Pompeian cinnabar paintings and mortars (House of Marcus Lucretius) with calcite, gypsum, calomel and wax; portable and benchtop Raman
notes: Three calcite numbers; calcite is a secondary phase. innoRam 785 nm (<300 mW) in situ and 785 (350 mW) and 532 nm (50 mW) lasers for samples. SI PDF included.

title: The study of Dominican amber-bearing sediments from Siete Cañadas and La Cumbre with a discussion on their origin
raman_evidence: PDF p.9 (Fig. 7E): calcite bands at 1083, 710, 279 and 152 cm-1 (aragonite 1083, 703, 204, 176, 150) in Raman spectra of the sediments; Mendeley Data deposit has the raw Raman spectra of calcite (SC4_calcite.CSV) and other minerals
sample_description: Mixed mineral fraction of Dominican amber-bearing sediments (calcite, aragonite, pyrite, anatase, hematite, quartz); micro-Raman
notes: Raw single-spectrum Raman CSVs (x = Raman shift 99-2500 cm-1, y = intensity) from Mendeley Data ydrbh8b33f (calcite SC4_calcite.CSV, aragonite SC1_aragonite.CSV, plus quartz, anatase, rutile, hematite, ilmenite, pyrite), copied to data/. The deposit also holds XRD, Rock-Eval, EDS and image files that were not downloaded.

title: Characterizing paint technologies and recipes in Levantine and Schematic rock art: El Carche site as a case study (Jalance, Spain)
raman_evidence: PDF p.21: substrate shows calcite bands at 1084, 711, 278 and 154 cm-1; nu3 broad band near 1440 cm-1 with 715 and 880 cm-1 in layers i and ii
sample_description: Micro-samples of Levantine and Schematic rock-art paint and calcareous substrate (El Carche, Jalance, Spain)
notes: Methods list '523 nm and 785 nm' lasers while the Results speak of 532 nm excitation (typo in the paper). SI PDF included.

title: Protection of the DNA from Selected Species of Five Kingdoms in Nature by Ba(II), Sr(II), and Ca(II) Silica–Carbonates: Implications about Biogenicity and Evolving from Prebiotic Chemistry to Biological Chemistry
raman_evidence: PDF pp.6-7 Table 2: calcite Raman bands per DNA type, e.g. 157, 283, 713, 1085 cm-1 (control, 5% CO2), 165, 291, 724, 1093 (control, RTP), 156, 282, 712, 1084 (E. coli, 5% CO2); other rows 156-172 / 282-291 / 712-724 / 1084-1093; SI Fig. S1
sample_description: Ca silica-carbonate biomorphs (calcite, some vaterite/aragonite) grown with DNA from five kingdoms under 5% CO2 or room temperature and pressure; Ba and Sr analogues in Tables 3 and 4
notes: Table 2 lists Raman (and IR) bands for 16 rows (8 DNA sets x 2 growth conditions, several also with aragonite or vaterite), with a large T/L/nu4/nu1 shift between the two growth conditions. Ba (witherite) and Sr (strontianite) tables are not calcite. SI PDF included.

title: Diagenesis Sequence and Hydrocarbon Accumulation Period of the Ordovician Reservoir in Well Tashen-6, Tahe Oilfield, Tarim Basin, NW China
raman_evidence: PDF p.6 (Fig. 6 caption): peaks at 2912.23 (methane) and 1086.48, 713.36, 281.90 and 154.84 cm-1 for the host fracture-filling calcite
sample_description: Fracture-filling calcite (Ordovician Penglaiba Formation, Tashen-6 well, Tarim Basin) hosting methane gas inclusions; laser Raman of inclusions
notes: Thermo DXR 2xi confocal Raman; the paper does not state the excitation wavelength. Four calcite positions with 0.01 cm-1 resolution printed in the caption. No SI.

title: CaCO3 loaded lipid microspheres prepared by the solid-in-oil-in-water emulsions technique with propylene glycol alginate and xanthan gum
raman_evidence: PDF p.12 (Fig. 7A): CaCO3 powder peaks at 1749.73, 1438.41, 1086.73, 713.54, 279.85 and 154.89 cm-1 (all six calcite modes)
sample_description: CaCO3 powder (calcite by XRD indexing) and its S/O/W lipid microsphere emulsions; Raman of powder, oil, water and emulsion phases
notes: The paper writes 'CaCO3 powders' and never names the polymorph; the six modes and the XRD indexing (012),(104),(110),(113),(202),(018),(116) identify calcite. Renishaw inVia-Qontor, 785 nm, 100 mW. No SI.

title: Facile extraction and characterization of calcium hydroxide from paper mill waste sludge of Bangladesh
raman_evidence: PDF p.9: pure CaCO3 peaks at 157.18, 280.95, 713.46 and 1087.53 cm-1; Ca(OH)2 at 359.72 and 1066.78 cm-1; the 1087.53 CaCO3 band grows as the 1066.78 band falls with air exposure
sample_description: CaCO3 and Ca(OH)2 extracted from paper-mill waste sludge, with air-exposure (carbonation) times 0-144 h
notes: Positions with two decimals ('approximately'); Horiba MacroRAM, 785 nm, <5 mW. The paper compares with the RRUFF calcite spectrum. Electronic supplementary material is on Figshare (collection c.6125262), not downloaded.

title: Multi-Technique Diagnostic Analysis of Plasters and Mortars from the Church of the Annunciation (Tortorici, Sicily)
raman_evidence: PDF p.4 (Fig. 2): preparation ground shows ~1080 with ~162, ~282, ~712 and ~1435 cm-1; PDF p.6 (Fig. 4d) and p.11 (Fig. 9b): calcite at ~153, ~280, ~712 and ~1087 cm-1
sample_description: Plasters, mortars, preparation ground and pigment layers of the Church of the Annunciation (Tortorici, Sicily); portable Raman
notes: Portable B&W Tek BTR111 Mini-Ram (785 nm). Calcite lattice and nu3 bands visible in several spectra (Figs. 2, 4, 9, 10). No SI.

title: Influence of Intramineral Proteins on the Growth of Carbonate Crystals Using as a Scaffold Membranes of Ratite Birds and Crocodiles Eggshells
raman_evidence: PDF p.7 Table 1 and p.9: Raman shifts of calcium silica-carbonate crystals for control and eight protein samples (control 161, 279, 713, 1081, 1436, 1748 cm-1; proteins 153-159, 279-283, 711-714, 1081-1090); Fig. 4
sample_description: Calcium silica-carbonate (calcite) biomorphs grown on ratite and crocodile eggshell membranes in the presence of intramineral proteins (struthiocalcins, crococalcins); Ba and Sr analogues in Tables 2 and 3
notes: Table 1 is a full Raman-shift table for 9 samples (also lists weak low bands near 94-115 cm-1). Tables 2 and 3 (Ba and Sr carbonates) are not calcite. SI zip holds one supplementary PDF.

title: Environmental impacts on the structural integrity of British rhodoliths
raman_evidence: PDF p.9: typical spectrum (S6) with four peaks indexed to high magnesian calcite at 166 (T), 288 (L), 720 (nu4) and 1092 (nu1) cm-1
sample_description: British rhodolith (coralline algae) skeletal high-Mg calcite; Raman used for Mg-calcite and dolomite check
notes: Mg-calcite example (all four peaks sit above the pure calcite values). Thermo DXRxi, 780 nm, 28 mW. Underlying data are in PANGAEA 10.1594/PANGAEA.899694 (large micro-CT zips, no Raman files) and data.bris. SI PDF included.

title: Room temperature bio-engineered multifunctional carbonates for CO2 sequestration and valorization
raman_evidence: PDF p.5 (Fig. 5a,b): peaks at about 161 (T, Eg), 288 (L, Eg), 718 (nu4, Eg) and 1091 (A1g) cm-1 of calcite; no extra aragonite L band
sample_description: Bio-engineered CaCO3 nanoparticles (plant-extract route) described as single-phase calcite; room-temperature Raman
notes: Nano-scale calcite with all four peaks several cm-1 above bulk values and explicit Eg/A1g assignments. The paper does not state the Raman excitation wavelength (the 240 nm quoted is for photoluminescence). SI PDF included.

title: Antibacterial Activity and Cell Viability of Biomimetic Magnesian Calcite Coatings on Biodegradable Mg
raman_evidence: PDF p.6 (Fig. 3b): calcite has dominant band at 1086 cm-1 and secondary bands at 711, 1433 and 1746 cm-1 assigned to A1g and Eg modes
sample_description: Calcite layer (biomimetic magnesian calcite coating) formed on biodegradable Mg by immersion in carbonated water; UV Raman
notes: UV excitation (325 nm, Horiba Jobin Yvon LabRam HR) gives nu3 (1433) and 2nu2 (1746) in the same spectrum; only 4 numbers, no lattice modes.

title: Formation of Natural Magnesium Silica Hydrate (M-S-H) and Magnesium Alumina Silica Hydrate (M-A-S-H) Cement
raman_evidence: PDF p.7 Fig. 6c caption: carbonate spectrum has peak pattern 154 w, 280 m, 712 m, 1085 s and 1435 w cm-1 diagnostic of calcite; quartz 463, 126, 205 cm-1
sample_description: Natural magnesium silicate hydrate (M-S-H/M-A-S-H) cement in veins and negative crystals of quartz with calcite; Raman spots on cement, quartz and carbonate
notes: Calcite pattern with relative intensity letters (w/m/s) printed in a caption. Laser 532.1 nm Spectra-Physics Millennia, 1.5 mW at sample, Olympus 100x. SI zip holds one supplementary PDF.

title: A new multi-analytical procedure for radiocarbon dating of historical mortars
raman_evidence: PDF p.10 Table 3: for five mortar powders calcite L 273.8-277.8, nu4 712.1-712.5 and nu1 1085.4-1086.0 cm-1 with FWHM (L 18.1-26.6, nu4 6.3-7.5, nu1 5.2-6.4 cm-1)
sample_description: Calcite mortar powders from historical mortars (geogenic vs anthropogenic calcite) for radiocarbon dating; micro-Raman of the same powder used for XRPD and ATR-FTIR
notes: Table 3 gives positions and FWHM for L, nu4 and nu1 (no T mode). Same research group as CAL023 and CAL024 but different samples (mortars from Italy). SI PDF included.

title: Scallop shells as biosorbents for water remediation from heavy metals: Contributions and mechanism of shell components in the adsorption of cadmium from aqueous matrix
raman_evidence: PDF p.10 (Fig. 7a): white shell shows only the bands at 1083, 707 and 274 cm-1 of the calcite matrix; pink and brown shells show two additional pigment bands
sample_description: White, pink and brown scallop shells (calcite matrix with pigments) used as Cd biosorbents; Raman before and after use
notes: He-Ne 632.8 nm, up to 20 mW. Calcite lattice band reads 274 cm-1 (lower than the usual 281-282). SI docx included.

title: Characterization of dolomite and calcite microcalcifications in human breast tissue†
raman_evidence: PDF p.8 (Fig. 5b): calcite nu4 712, nu1 1085 and lattice modes at 156 and 280 cm-1; Fig. 6 compares MC spectra with commercial calcite and biogenic magnesian calcite
sample_description: Calcite and dolomite microcalcifications in human breast tissue (DCIS), compared with reference calcite and biogenic Mg-calcite
notes: Nd:YAG 532 nm, 3.5 mW. Raman phase statistics in a table (83.2% of MCs are calcite). SI PDF included.

title: A study of bacteria producing carbonic anhydrase enzyme for CaCO3 precipitation and soil biocementation
raman_evidence: PDF p.9 (Fig. 10a): bioprecipitate and control spectra match calcite with primary peak at 1088 cm-1 and further peaks at 280, 153 and 715 cm-1
sample_description: CaCO3 bioprecipitates from carbonic-anhydrase-producing bacteria and a chemical control, for soil biocementation
notes: Horiba LabRAM ARAMIS, 633 nm (1% power), 600 l/mm. SI: genome-tree tsv and PDF, CA protein sequences and calcium-consumption figure as docx (no Raman data).

title: A large intraplate hydrogen-rich hydrothermal system driven by serpentinization in the western Pacific: Kunlun
raman_evidence: PDF p.3: on-site in situ laser Raman detected peaks at 281, 713 and 1084 cm-1 typical of calcite; Figshare workbook 'Raman data of carbonatites' has raw spectra (sheets dark yellow rock (dolomite) and authigenic carbonate (calcite))
sample_description: Authigenic carbonate (calcite) and dolomite rock from the Kunlun hydrothermal field (serpentinization-driven, western Pacific); on-site in situ laser Raman
notes: Raw Raman spectra (Raman shift about 100-4350 cm-1 vs intensity, one sheet per rock type) from Figshare 10.6084/m9.figshare.29095904, copied to data/. Kaiser Optical in situ spectrometer with 532 nm Nd laser (150 mW). Both sheets peak at 281 and 1084 cm-1 (the sheet named dolomite is calcite-like by its peak positions); only three calcite numbers in the text. SI movies (zip) not kept.

title: An unfinished Pompeian construction site reveals ancient Roman building technology
raman_evidence: PDF p.6: calcite shows nu1 at about 1085 cm-1 and lattice modes at about 280 and 155 cm-1; aragonite shows 1085, nu4 doublet 701/706, 208 and 152 cm-1
sample_description: Mortar and binder samples from an unfinished Pompeian construction site (calcite with aragonite)
notes: WITec UHTS, Nd:YAG 532 nm, 600 g/mm, calibrated on the Si 520 cm-1 line. Approximate (~) positions. Three SI PDFs included.

title: Alumina nanoparticle-induced decarbonation at subduction-zone conditions
raman_evidence: PDF p.4 Fig. 3 caption: calcite identified by peaks at 154, 280, 712, 1086 and 1437 cm-1 (aragonite 152, 178, 207, 248, 704, 1085, 1464) in Raman spectra of high P-T run products; Zenodo workbook sheet Fig.3 holds the raw spectra
sample_description: Calcite/aragonite from CaCO3 + Al2O3 (nano or micron) or Al(OH)3 piston-cylinder runs at 0.5-2.8 GPa and 350-1050 C; ex situ Raman of the recovered samples
notes: P-T series. Raw Raman spectra (sheet Fig.3, about 88-3900 cm-1; calcite peaks at about 155, 281, 712, 1086 cm-1 in the 0.5 GPa runs and aragonite-type 151, 206, 1084 in the 2.0 GPa run; run labels 0.5GPa-600C, 0.5GPa-850C, 2.0GPa-650C, 2.8GPa-1050C, nano vs micron Al2O3) are in the Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.15767718 workbook copied to data/ (sheet Fig.2 is XRD). Per the text calcite is the product at 0.5 GPa and 350-850 C, CaCO3 becomes aragonite at 2.0 GPa/650 C and amorphous at 2.8 GPa/1050 C; the Fig. 3 caption gives both calcite and aragonite peak sets. SI: two PDFs.

title: Spatially decoupled electrochemical strategy for lime passivation prevention and sustainable phosphate recovery
raman_evidence: PDF p.7: Raman of post-use limestone shows calcite nu1 1087 plus 155, 282 and 714 cm-1 (Fig. 4g); Source Data sheet Fig. 4g has the raw spectra (pristine and post-use limestone, 98-2000 cm-1)
sample_description: Limestone (calcite) before and after use as Ca source in limestone-integrated electrolysis for phosphate recovery (brushite formation)
notes: Raw Raman spectra in Source Data workbook (SI MOESM3 xlsx, copied to data/): sheet Fig. 4g, columns Raman shift, Pristine limestone, Post-use limestone (Thermo DXR3, 2 cm-1 resolution; the sheet spans 98-2000 cm-1 and peaks at 156.2, 281.6, 713.5, 1087.7 for pristine limestone). The paper labels the 282 band nu2 (it is the lattice L mode). Other sheets are XRD and process data.

title: Mineralized carbonates contribute to the millennial durability of Roman concrete
raman_evidence: PDF p.4 (Fig. 3H): calcite at 279 (molecular motion), 711 (bending), 1084 and 1432 cm-1
sample_description: Lime binder and lime clasts of a Roman concrete latrine sample (carbonated calcite)
notes: 532 nm, about 5 mW, backscattering. SI PDF included; the SI movies zip was not kept.
